newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CFTC to help review heating oil market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CFTC to help review heating oil market.

text.p: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Tuesday it was working with the Energy Department to review what impact heating oil futures trading might be having on heating oil stocks.

Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary called for the study last Friday after meeting with top oil industry executives to discuss ways to prevent a heating oil price shock this winter, with heating oil inventories at historically low levels.

"Issues have been raised by market participants about the possible effects of the futures markets on heating oil inventories, and the DOE (Energy Department) has promised to analyze the situation," the CFTC said.

Oil analysts have suggested that speculation in futures markets has deepened the market's backwardation, in which prices in near months are higher than outer months, which in turn has discouraged refiners from building stocks because they expect product prices to fall.

The CFTC said while it had not reached any conclusion on the issue, "it appears to the (CFTC's) staff that price changes in the heating oil futures market have been influenced only by economic factors relating to supply and demand."
